titulo: Dativo 2: the verbs that take the dative: Helfen, danken, gehören

aula.titulo: Dativo 2: the verbs that take the dative
aula.objetivo: Use the verbs that take the dative for the person (helfen, danken, gehören, gefallen, schmecken, passen, fehlen, antworten, gratulieren, glauben) and the expressions of sensation with «mir» and «dir».

blocos.titulo: Verbs that take the dative: the person goes into the dative, step by step
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: some German verbs take the DATIVE for the person, even when in English the object looks direct: «Ich helfe dir» (I help you), «Ich danke dir» (I thank you), «Das Buch gehört mir» (the book belongs to me). STEP 2: these verbs do NOT use the accusative for the person: saying «Ich helfe dich» is wrong. STEP 3: memorise the verb together with «wem?»: «helfen + dative», «danken + dative», «gehören + dative». STEP 4: «helfen» changes e to i in the «du» and the «er» (du hilfst, er hilft). STEP 5: «gratulieren» takes «zu» + dative for the reason: «Ich gratuliere dir zum Geburtstag.» STEP 6: «antworten» takes the dative for the person and «auf» + accusative for what is answered: «Er antwortet dem Chef auf die E-Mail.»
blocos.comparacao: In English we say «I help you» and «I thank you», where the person looks like a direct object. In German the rule is fixed: with «helfen», «danken» and «gehören», the person ALWAYS goes into the dative.

tabela.en: We congratulate you on your birthday.

blocos.enunciado: Say 6 sentences with «helfen», «danken» and «gehören»: «Ich helfe meiner Mutter. Das Handy gehört mir.»
Write the pronouns in the dative for the nine persons and 5 sentences with them.
